one_month_reasoning: Unlike the 2026-09-29 window, this one (to Nov 5) very likely contains the Q3-26 print: Trefis and the Thursday-after-close pattern point to Oct 29, but Amazon has not yet posted its webcast notice (press center checked Oct 6), so it is still an estimate. That leaves ~5 sessions of post-earnings trading inside the window. The bar: Amazon guided Q3 sales $197-202B (+9-12%, held down by Prime Day moving into June) and operating income $22.5-26.5B (8-K Ex.99.1). Yahoo consensus has revenue at $202.03B, the top of the guided range, and EPS at $1.95 (flat y/y as reported). So a beat on revenue alone is not enough; AWS growth vs the Q2 37% and the first 2027 capex number will set the reaction. Also in the window: the Oct 27-28 FOMC, where Polymarket prices a hike at only 19.5% (no change 80.5%, ~$26.9M traded, Oct 5). Hike odds collapsed after the weak September jobs report, which removes most of the two-sided rate shock I carried last week, but the 10-year sits at 5.31%, a 24-year high. Microsoft and Alphabet report in late October (estimated Oct 27-28) with cloud and capex read-through, and Prime Big Deal Days (Oct 6-7) is not a mover. I have no directional edge on the print: Q3 OI guidance implies +29-52% y/y, but the headline sales slowdown can be misread. So I center at ~$257 (+0.4%, carry only) and widen the tails for the earnings gap: a mixture of 80% sigma 9.5% (34%/3.5 ~ 9.7%) and 20% sigma 17%. That gives P(>=spot) 0.515 and P(>=$307.55) 0.054.

fair_value.method: 50/50 blend of forward P/E at the horizon ($298 = NTM EPS at Oct-2027 ~$12.68 [25% FY27 consensus $10.51 + 75% FY28 $13.40] x 23.5x) and a horizon SOTP ($282 = AWS NTM after-tax OI ~$76.0B x 26 = $1.98T + retail/ads ~$46.6B x 22 = $1.02T + Anthropic stake after tax ~$0.16T - consensus net debt at Oct-2027 ~$61B - Globalstar ~$11B, over 10.95B shares).

inputs_detail.derivation: S&P Global consensus via stockanalysis; up from $8.15 on Sep 30. Excludes Anthropic mark-to-market gains that inflate GAAP FY26 ($12.88 per Yahoo/MarketScreener).
Yahoo EPS trend: $10.51 now vs $10.50 7 and 30 days ago, $9.99 90 days ago; 4 up / 0 down revisions in 30 days. MarketScreener shows the same $10.51.

$13.81 consensus less ~$0.43: the standing AI-capex view puts Big-4 2027 capex ~10% above consensus (Amazon 2027 consensus $256.5-319.1B in that file, $277.4B on MarketScreener), so I assume ~$33B more 2027 capex than MarketScreener consensus (~$310B base). At a ~5.5-year average asset life (judgment) that adds ~$6B of 2028 D&A, i.e. $6B x (1-21%) / 10.95B = $0.43/share. Rounded to $13.40 (+27.5%).

Peer median (11 names, FY~CY2027 basis) is 26.7x, range 13.6-77.8x. The mega-cap cloud subgroup (MSFT 26.7, GOOGL 23.2, META 21.8, ORCL 15.6) has a median of 22.5x. AMZN itself trades at 23.9x 2027E at the Oct-5 reference price. 23.5x sits 12% below the all-peer median and slightly above the cloud-subgroup median. The discount reflects negative group FCF (consensus -$34.0B 2026, -$8.2B 2027, turning positive only in 2028 at +$35.7B) and net debt rising ($22.3B to $74.0B to $104.0B 2026-28), both persisting through the horizon, plus a 5.31% 10-year yield. The small premium over the cloud subgroup reflects faster EPS growth (+26%/+31% FY27/FY28 vs +16-20% for MSFT/GOOGL/META). Unchanged from 2026-09-29.

methods.name: SOTP
methods.inputs: Horizon (NTM at Oct-2027) after-tax OI: AWS 0.25 x 2027 $82.8B + 0.75 x 2028 $100.6B = $96.2B pre-tax, x 0.79 x 26 = $1.975T; North America+International 0.25 x $53B + 0.75 x $61B = $59.0B, x 0.79 x 22 = $1.025T; Anthropic after tax $0.16T; less net debt ~$61B and Globalstar ~$10.9B; 10.95B diluted shares; total ~$3.088T = $282/share

inputs_detail.input: AWS H1-2026 revenue / OI; Q2 AWS revenue / OI

inputs_detail.derivation: 2026E ~$174B (H1 $79.8B + H2 ~$94B at the ~$169B run-rate management cited, rising) x 1.32. The call says power capacity doubles by end-2027 vs 2025 and 2027 capacity is 'largely reserved'. Margin is held below Q2's 39.3% because the call says Q2 included derivative gains (+650bp y/y, +520bp ex gains) and D&A is ramping with ~$220B 2026 capex. Carried over from 2026-09-29; inputs re-verified.

Growth decelerates from ~32% to 25% as the 2027 capacity doubling laps. The call says 'quite a bit of capacity' is already reserved for 2028, and the backlog is $496B (10-Q RPO). The margin dips 1pt for D&A from the higher capex path (source 32). Group consensus revenue +15.8% in 2028 (MarketScreener $947.9B to $1,097.4B) is consistent with AWS growing well above group.

H1-26 NA+Intl OI $20.5B reported. Q3-26 total OI guide $22.5-26.5B less ~$17B AWS gives retail ~$5.5-9.5B, and Q4 seasonality gives ~$43-45B for 2026E. +18% for 2027 (ads mix, fulfilment efficiency) gives ~$53B. 2028 +15% tracks consensus group revenue growth of +15.8% at flat margin.

Near Microsoft's 26.7x FY27 P/E (the closest scaled cloud peer), above Alphabet 23.2x and Oracle 15.6x. Justified by faster growth (AWS ~25-32% vs the peers' +20% EPS) and a $496B backlog. Not higher, because AWS is losing share to Google Cloud and Azure. Inside the 13.6-77.8x peer range; unchanged.

Retail/e-commerce peer median P/E is 33x (WMT 33.0, COST 40.5, MELI 33.0, SHOP 77.8, SE 23.6, CPNG 40.2, BABA 13.6), range 13.6-77.8x. I raised this from 20x on 2026-09-29 now that a peer set is required, but it stays a third below the median for three reasons. WMT and COST carry a low-cyclicality staples premium with dividends and buybacks; Amazon has no dividend and only $6.1B of repurchase authorization, and group FCF is negative. Regulatory overhang runs through the horizon: the FTC monopolization trial starts Mar 29, 2027, and the FTC/22-state ad-auction suit was filed Aug 31, 2026. And the Q3 sales guide of +9-12% shows discretionary/calendar sensitivity.

bear.story: AI capex digestion or share loss: AWS growth slides toward the low 20s while $280-310B 2027 capex lifts D&A, so FY28 EPS lands near $11.5 instead of $13.4. Consensus FCF stays negative into 2027 and net debt climbs past $74B with the 10-year above 5%. The multiple compresses to ~18x NTM EPS of ~$11 (~$198). Q3/Q4 prints disappoint against a revenue consensus already at the top of the guide, and the FTC trial (Mar 29, 2027) and ad-auction suit weigh.

base.story: Consensus broadly delivered: FY27 EPS ~$10.5 (+26%) and FY28 ~$13.4 (+27%) as AWS grows ~30% on capacity that is already reserved, with retail/ads up mid-teens. FCF turns toward positive in 2028. The multiple drifts from ~24x to ~22-23.5x NTM as rates stay high. This is set slightly below my $290 fair value to shrink toward the market for model error, because most of this week's fair-value rise came from method and consensus inputs, not news.

bull.story: AWS holds 35%+ as capacity doubles and Trainium gains external customers, and capex discipline shows in 2027 (FCF inflects early). An Anthropic IPO at or above $2T talk re-marks the $190B stake upward. The multiple holds ~25-26x on NTM EPS ~$13.5-14 (consensus FY28 $13.81 delivered), toward the $330.59 sell-side mean and beyond.

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E 13.6x (BABA) to 77.8x (SHOP); forward EV/EBITDA 7.76x (ORCL) to 53.2x (SHOP). 11 peers, all from MarketScreener consensus valuation pages at Oct-5 reference prices, using the fiscal year closest to calendar 2027 (FY ending Jun-2027 to May-2028). Next-year growth is the EPS growth of the following fiscal year, derived from the ratio of consecutive-year P/Es at the same price.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 23.5x NTM P/E at the horizon vs the 26.7x peer median (12% discount) and a 22.5x mega-cap cloud-subgroup median (MSFT/GOOGL/META/ORCL). AMZN itself is at 23.9x 2027E P/E and 10.2x 2027E EV/EBITDA (below the 13.5x median, because heavy capex inflates EBITDA relative to earnings), so I hold the current multiple rather than assume a re-rating. SOTP: AWS at 26x (≈MSFT 26.7x), retail/ads at 22x (vs retail-peer median 33x).
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: The discount to the all-peer median rests on features that persist through Oct-2027 per consensus. Group FCF is negative (-$34.0B 2026E, -$8.2B 2027E; positive only in 2028E at $35.7B), while MSFT/GOOGL/META/WMT/COST are FCF-positive. Net debt rises from $22.3B to $74.0B over 2026-27E with the 10-year at 5.31%. And the WMT/COST staples premium (33-40x on ~10% growth) does not transfer to discretionary-heavy Amazon retail facing the FTC trial (Mar 2027) and the ad-auction suit. A deeper discount is not justified, because consensus EPS growth (+26% FY27, +31% FY28) exceeds every mega-cap peer's. I do not use sell-side outperformance calls as justification.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$185 (28% under spot, under the $196 52-week low) the stock would trade at ~17.6x FY27 consensus EPS of $10.51, which is still being revised up (4 up / 0 down in 30 days) and growing ~26%. That is ~35% below the 26.7x peer median and below Meta's 21.8x despite faster growth. Such a level is consistent only with the market pricing an impairment of AWS backlog quality (renegotiated OpenAI/Anthropic commitments), AWS growth falling to the low 20s, or a structural depreciation-driven margin reset, not 34%-vol noise or a rate de-rating. Unchanged from 2026-09-29.

reasoning: Delta refresh of my 2026-09-29 view ($263 FV, P(>=247) 0.59). What changed in the evidence: (1) No new 8-K/10-Q since Sep 29; EDGAR shows only a Form 4 (a $251.5k 10b5-1 sale by Herrington). The pre-Sep-29 filings I had missed are the GBP 4.25B notes (FWP Sep 9, closed Sep 14 per 8-K, listed on Nasdaq per 8-A12B Sep 24) and a new director (Mandia, 8-K 5.02). The notes raise gross debt and confirm continued debt funding of capex, but are net-neutral at issue. (2) The stock rose 3.9% (246.67 to 256.33) vs QQQ +2.9%, MSFT +4.0%, GOOGL +2.0%, ORCL +5.1%, META flat. That is mostly beta to a Nasdaq at record highs after weak payrolls cut October hike odds to ~20% (Polymarket, $26.9M). There was no company-specific news: the press center shows only AWS customer releases, and the TD Cowen Buy reiteration was a non-event. (3) Consensus edged up: FY26 normalized $8.15 to $8.31, FY27 $10.48 to $10.51 (Yahoo, 4 up / 0 down in 30 days), and I now have a sourced FY28 consensus of $13.81 (MarketScreener), where last week I used my own +20% ($12.56). (4) The new peer-set rule: 11 comps on one FY~CY2027 basis (median 26.7x P/E, 13.5x EV/EBITDA). (5) Method fixes: the SOTP is now rolled to horizon NTM earnings, consistent with the P/E leg; last week it applied today's forward multiples to 2027 earnings, which is a value as of today rather than at the horizon. Net debt now uses the consensus path to Oct-2027 (~$61B) instead of a Q2 proxy (~$31B), and the retail multiple rose from 20x to 22x to stay defensibly inside the peer range. Result: P/E $282 to $298 (FY28 input $12.56 to $13.40, multiple 23.5x unchanged), SOTP $244 to $282, FV $263 to $290. I do not move the forecast distribution all the way to the FV: most of the +$27 is inputs and method, not news, and FV estimates are noisy, so the ladder uses a three-component lognormal mixture (medians 198/280/355, weights 25/50/25, sigmas 0.30/0.19/0.24). That gives a median of ~$278 (+8.5%), mean ~$286, and log-sd ~0.31, close to the 34% realized vol (slightly below, since the dispersion of scenario medians already adds spread). P(>=256) is 0.618 and P(>=449) 0.045. Source mix: the 11 required comp pages and consensus pages push the in-lane share to 12/32 (~38%). Among non-comp sources it is 12/21 (~57%), below the 60% target because the comp rule requires a data page per peer. Lane-unique items: the GBP notes FWP/8-K/8-A12B, the Item 5.02 8-K, the Form 4 and the 10-Q note detail. Not used (unverified): CNN on Anthropic IPO timing (HTTP 451), payroll figures (secondary only), and Microsoft/Alphabet report dates beyond Trefis's estimate.
